name: metaballs
summary: Full-bleed hero running Paper Shaders' metaballs on WebGL2: ten coloured blobs travelling and merging into one organic mass on black, off-centre so the copy sits beside it, over a matched CSS blob field.

colors.description: Up to seven blob colours. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c5 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette. Upstream default preset.

speed.description: Rate the blobs travel. 0 renders a single static frame. Forced to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

count.description: How many blobs are in the field.

size.description: Blob radius; high enough and neighbours merge into one another rather than passing.

deviations.what: u_offsetX is 0.34; every upstream metaballs preset uses 0 or -0.3.
deviations.why: The merged mass sits dead centre at offset 0, right under the headline. 0.34 moves it right (measured: negative moves left) so the copy column has the left half of the section to itself. Upstream's own backgroundPreset offsets for the same reason, in the other direction.

deviations.what: The noise texture is decoded before ShaderMount is constructed, so the shader starts one microtask later than a React mount would.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream's React component hands getShaderNoiseTexture() straight to ShaderMount and re-renders when it loads; a vanilla mount has no re-render, and ShaderMount throws on an image that is not complete. The image is a data: URI, so nothing is fetched.
